subject: Hospitality
title: The Burj Al Arab: A Sail in the Sea
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Burj Al Arab: A Sail in the Sea.

hook.text: Dubai's Burj Al Arab stands on an artificial island shaped like a sail. It was designed to be the city's icon—and it worked.

buildup.text: Tom Wright of Atkins designed it so the silhouette would be recognizable from any angle.

discovery.text: The building is 321 meters tall—one of the world's tallest hotels. Its helipad doubles as a tennis court 210 meters above the sea.

twist.text: The Burj Al Arab calls itself '7-star' but no official 7-star rating exists. The label was invented by a journalist.

climax.text: The hotel's architecture IS its brand. Remove the building and the brand has nothing. Design and identity are inseparable.

punchline.text: No 7-star rating exists. But the building made the world believe it does.

quiz.question: Is the Burj Al Arab officially rated as a 7-star hotel?
options: Yes, by the World Tourism Organization
No—a journalist invented the label and it stuck
